To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed dataset and evaluation methodology enable a more accurate and comprehensive analysis of the current state-of-the-art in the area of video segmentation.

(i) the DAVIS dataset is the first large scale dataset for video object segmentation; (ii) DAVIS contains dense pixel-accurate ground truth segmentation annotations; (iii) the DAVIS benchmark enables a comprehensive evaluation and comparison of current video object segmentation methods; and (iv) the results reveal strengths and weaknesses of existing methods and open up promising directions for further research.

the new benchmark dataset and the new evaluation metrics provide the following insights: (1) the current state-of-the-art methods are able to produce accurate segmentations of moving objects in videos with a high level of detail, but they still fail to produce perfect results, (2) there is still a significant gap between the performance of the best method and the ground truth, (3) the best performing methods are still not capable to handle the challenging cases of motion blur, fast motion and appearance changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

two main objectives: (a) to provide a new benchmark dataset to facilitate research and evaluation in video object segmentation, and (b) to present a comprehensive analysis of state-of-the-art approaches and provide a set of evaluation metrics to guide the future research.

two important questions in video object segmentation: 1) What are the most challenging video sequences for the task? and 2) How should we evaluate the performance of video object segmentation algorithms? We hope that our work will provide answers to both questions and will enable the development of better algorithms for this important computer vision task.

three main contributions: (1) A new, high quality dataset and benchmark for video object segmentation, (2) a comprehensive analysis of the performance of state-of-the-art approaches, and (3) a novel evaluation methodology that is more comprehensive than existing approaches.
